items.label: Open source with identified code/content licences
Cite the research software separately from the host educational repository
Restored reference R environment reproduces a frozen synthetic RNA-seq case
Statistical nominal FDR control at 5% under tested RNA-seq scenarios
Original 2,100 R fit records and empirical study summaries independently SHA-checked
Frozen software source and all benchmark CSVs preserved under a long-lived DOI
Multi-omics benefit over best mono-omic baselines on independent matched subjects
New independent laboratory/cohort reproduces frozen preprocessing and conclusions
Real novice users and keyboard/screen-reader testers have demonstrated usability
Separately installable, versioned and maintained research software release
Journal public-development-history and impact requirements independently verified
Human author review of all code, scientific claims, AI-assisted text and acknowledgements

notes: This is an auditable readiness register; successful software CI never sets automatic_publication_ready to true.
Evidence present in an open PR does not mean code is deployed to main.
No novel biological association or clinical efficacy has been established by these synthetic benchmarks.
The 5% nominal FDR is not demonstrated by the two observed DESeq2 benchmark campaigns.
